Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • The 3-D plant is built from layout.json at true scale.
  • Twelve stations follow the flow: air, sulfur, furnace, boiler, converter, absorbers.
  • 485 m to station 12, with a climb to +22.7 on R-201.
  • 77 reading points sit on 12 levels.

2 · Reading a dial · pick a gauge, move the reading

Where does the design value sit?

Dial range: 0 to the next round number ≥ 1.5 × design.

The design value sits between about a third and two thirds of the scale, so a needle near either end is worth a second look.

2 · Reading a dial

Close-up: transmitter and local gauge

3 · Hand-valve states and seals

Four states, two of them sealed

Reading changes nothing; turning a valve changes the plant.

StateMeaningHere
NOopen, operable7
NCclosed, operable1
LOsealed open: permit to break4
LCchained, locked closed1

3 · Hand valves · pick a valve

Thirteen valves, and what each one guards

P = proposed by the layout (assumed); three added for the steam and BFW systems.

A sealed valve stays in its state without a permit; an operable valve acts on the running plant.

4 · A valve acts on the plant · model runs, SIS armed

Closing a running pump's discharge

A dead-headed pump trips at once; what follows depends on the spare and on the trips behind it.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • Transmitters show the DCS value; local gauges show what only the field shows.
  • On a dial ranged to ≥ 1.5 × design, the design value sits a third to two thirds up.
  • NO and NC valves are operable; LO and LC need a permit.
  • A closed discharge trips a running pump; the spare or a trip follows.

1 · Reading a tag · ISA 5.1

First letter: what is measured

F · T · P
flow · temperature · pressure
1st
PD · A · L
pressure difference · analysis · level
1st

hand · shut-off (safety) · position
1st
E · T · G

next

Read left to right: FT = flow transmitter, PDG = pressure-difference gauge.

The number is the loop: FE-100 and FT-100 measure one flow.

1 · Reading a tag · pick one

Letters say what, numbers say where

The converter is the 200 series: bed 1 is 201, 202, 203 (inlet, middle, exit); bed 2 is 211, 212, 213.

2 · The rounds sheet

The outside operator's log

StationRows (examples)
1total air · discharge pressure · blower state
2pump states · stand-by filter valve · gauge
6–8bed temperatures · pressure drop · HV-112
11–12acid flows · spare pump · stack SO₂

28 rows: 21 numbers, 7 states.

Checked against the live plant: read and check in one round.

3 · Tolerance · write a value

When does a written reading count as right?

$|r - v| \le \max(\tau,\;0.02\,|v|)$
$r$
value you wrote
unit
$v$
plant value now
unit
$\tau$
row tolerance
unit

The band is the larger of the two: FT-301, AT-306 and PDT-224 get their row τ, most others 2 %.

4 · Field against DCS

Why walk, when the DCS shows it all?

Only in the field

Local gauges, hand-valve positions, seals, levels in glasses, leaks, noise.

Both, independently

A control valve's real stroke; a pump really running.

Logged

Every reading, check and valve move goes to the event log as OPER.

Verify a device in the field before trusting the loop it drives.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • Tag letters give the variable and the device; the number gives the loop.
  • The rounds sheet has 28 rows, two or three per station.
  • A value counts within max(τ, 2 %) of the plant now.
  • The field shows what the DCS cannot: gauges, valves, seals.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the round in flow order and reach every level.

2

Read each gauge against where its design value sits on the dial.

3

Never move a sealed valve without a permit.

4

Before closing a valve, know which pump or trip sits behind it.

5

Write every reading at once, with its tag.
